items.title: Eddie Miller and Pete Fountain Interview, 1970-01-09
items.q: Oh, look at Lloyd. Just always, since I was a kid, I mean, there was no way there was any color situation in any way.

ctx.x: What do you think about that, Eddie, about the influence between white and black musicians?

Oh, I think this is one of the first things that happened, I think, you speak about this, about integration. I think that musicians, white and black, they were the first to get together, and there was never any... Oh, look at Lloyd. Just always, since I was a kid, I mean, there was no way there was any color situation in any way.

Mr. Fountain, another question. You mentioned earlier that in your records, you often have to play the tunes that the public wants. Well, isn't that also a pressure down in the club? Maybe you said you play the Sains every night because they want it. Don't you have to play the tunes that the people, they're buying the drinks, they're paying to come in, and isn't it difficult sometimes to play something that perhaps you would want to play that is not familiar to your customers?
